title: DC-area forecast: Warming up through Friday; watching weekend rain chances
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: A nice mix of sun and clouds as morning temperatures rise into and through the 60s to low 70s, topping out near 80 this afternoon.

What’s next? Heating up well into the 80s Thursday and Friday. Cooler this weekend as rain chances rise, but how quickly and how high they rise is uncertain.

Today’s daily digit — 8/10: Not too far off from an ideal fall day. Just a touch too warm and not super dry air. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Wednesday): Warming up nicely under partly sunny skies, with afternoon highs in the upper 70s to low 80s. Light winds from the southwest add a hint of humidity with dew points in the low 60s. Confidence: High 😎 Nice Day!

Tonight: Partly cloudy with comfortable evening readings falling back to near 70. Overnight lows in the upper 50s to mid-60s with light winds. Confidence: High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Thursday): Mostly sunny as the warm-up continues. Highs reach the mid- to upper 80s with light winds from the southwest, and still with that touch of humidity (dew points in the low 60s). Confidence: High

Tomorrow night: Mostly clear and mild with lows in the 60s. Confidence: High

A look ahead

Friday starts mostly sunny in the morning with some increasing afternoon clouds. It should be the warmest day of the week with highs in the mid-80s to near 90. A cold front approaching from the northwest could bring a few showers by Friday evening or overnight. Confidence: Medium-High

That cold front has a shot to push far enough south of us Saturday to leave us with just the chance of isolated showers, although some models keep the front closer by with a higher rain chance. Highs should be in the low to mid-70s with partly to mostly cloudy skies. Confidence: Low-Medium

Showers or a period of rain may end up more likely Saturday night and Sunday as the front comes back north. But models aren't locked into this scenario quite yet. Expect plenty of clouds Sunday with highs in the mid-60s to low 70s. Confidence: Low

DC weather history for September 30

Remnants of Tropical Storm Nicole in 2010 unleashed a record 4.66 inches of rain, causing widespread flooding and even spawning a weak tornado in the region.
